title: Mechanisms of the development of chronic lung disease in very preterm infants - a prospective observational cohort study
summary: The Ulm BPD study investigates the causes and mechanisms of chronic lung disease (BPD) in very preterm infants. The aim is to analyze the interactions between various risk factors, clinical treatments, and biological samples to gain a better understanding of the disease's origins. This is intended to help develop new, more effective treatment methods in the long term.

interventions.name: Main Observation Group: Very preterm infants (VLBW infants) born at ≤ 32+0 weeks of gestation at the Perinatal Center Ulm. This group is observed throughout their entire stay in the neonatal intensive care unit (NICU) and the follow-up unit until final discharge or transfer.
Control Group: Healthy term-born newborns: This group serves as a reference for the physiological state at birth. Clinical data are collected to assess exposures.

Control Group: Pregnant women with intact pregnancies: This group includes women undergoing amniocentesis or fetal interventions, providing unique biosample-related data on the prenatal pathology of preterm birth.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
- Gestational Age: All very preterm infants (VLBW infants) born at ≤ 32+0 weeks of gestation at the Perinatal Center Ulm.
- Healthy Term-Born Newborns: Newborns who are healthy and born at term.
- Pregnant Women with Intact Pregnancies: Pregnant women undergoing amniocentesis or fetal interventions.
Exclusion criteria:
- Severe congenital malformations: According to international classification systems, excluding inguinal hernias, PDA, atrial septal defects, ventricular septal defects, and all congenital anomalies that do not affect pulmonary, cardiovascular, and psychomotor capacities.
- Severe genetic disorders: Excluding genetic disorders that are not relevant to pulmonary, cardiovascular, and psychomotor outcomes.
- Severe metabolic diseases: Excluding hyperglycemia of the preterm infant.
- Birth before 22+0 weeks of gestation.
- Palliative care decision: Before inclusion in the study.
- No parental consent.
- Withdrawal of consent.
